It is cosmetic here: the operator directly measured this K-quant path at 80-90% of a 220 GB/s readbw ceiling, so it achieves near-peak DRAM bandwidth and is DRAM-bandwidth-bound, not VNNI/issue-bound; the 256-bit body needs only ~0.5 IPC per 64 B weight chunk vs a ~2 IPC EPYC core (~3x headroom), so halving its vector-instruction count cannot clear the enforced 1.544% decode floor. The operator has retired every other lever that moves a bandwidth-bound GEMM on this host (streaming/MLP/prefetch, thread count, barrier/sync/spin, dispatch/affinity, batch/ubatch), and the single remaining lever on this path, bytes via dense requantization (H2), is a requantized-model target revision, not a kernel-source patch this loop can build, gate and A/B. No admissible kernel-source hypothesis has a payoff the existing matched A/B can demonstrate above the floor.

hypothesis.statement: In ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_gemm_kquants.cpp, the Q4_K GEMM mul_mat_qX_K_q8_2_X4_T<DequantizerQ4K_AVX2, nrc_y> (top patchable symbol, ~22.5% of sampled user cycles on the selected run) is 256-bit-only: Q4Bits_AVX2 unpacks the 4-bit weights into four ymm via _mm256_and/_mm256_srli, and the inner loop does _mm256_dpbusd_epi32 (or _mm256_maddubs_epi16) plus a 6-instruction horizontal reduction per 128-element subblock. This build is -march=native on a Zen5 EPYC 9655 with AVX512F/VNNI/VL/BW/DQ, so HAVE_FANCY_SIMD is already defined in this TU, but this kernel never uses 512-bit. Add an in-place HAVE_FANCY_SIMD branch that unpacks the Q4_K 4-bit weights into zmm (512-bit) and computes the dot with _mm512_dpbusd_epi32 and a 512-bit reduction, keeping the existing 256-bit code as the non-AVX512 fallback. This halves the instruction count of the dequant+dot inner loop and doubles ALU work per instruction. Q4_K has the heaviest dequant of this model's matmul paths (6-bit scales+mins+4-bit unpack), so - unlike the Q8_0/MXFP4 paths the operator measured at 80-94% of the bandwidth ceiling and retired as bandwidth-bound - this path is the one most likely to be ALU-bound and to gain from vector width. Only the Q4_K dequantizer and the Q4_K/Q5_K template body change; the selector (iqk_set_kernels_kquants) and all shared/header helpers are untouched.

abstain: No admissible kernel-source mechanism has an honest payoff. The two dominant ops are memory-bound at the measured host read-BW ceiling: MUL_MAT dense (Q8_0, ~43.5% wall, 18.3% user-cycles, 80% of the 220 GB/s ceiling) and MUL_MAT_ID MoE (Q4_K, ~42% wall, the single largest kernel at 22.5% user-cycles via mul_mat_qX_K_q8_2_X4_T<DequantizerQ4K_AVX2>, 90% of ceiling), each already reading the minimum on-disk weight bytes; the compute share of these memory-bound GEMV-ish ops is a small minority (~6%), so the only compute-throughput edit available in an admitted route (the Q4_K/Q5_K dot body) is a cosmetic variant expected to land at/under the enforced 1.544% decode floor, i.e. no mechanism, and the MoE slab scheduling (iqk_mul_mat_moe_rows) is already optimized per the INF-70 B3-k note. The levers the bundle shows have real headroom (dense-Q8 requantization, H2 rank-1; engram-table requantization; pruning F32) are model-artifact changes ('a new target revision, not an in-place arm'), not llama.cpp kernel source, so out of scope for a kernel optimisation. The remaining candidates are explicitly DEAD on arrival in the bundle: barrier/sync/idle-spin (the 50% user-cycle family), prefetch/MLP/streaming-efficiency, work-dispatch granularity, thread count, NUMA thread policy. The other admitted CPU routes (GATED_DELTA_NET, iqk_moe_fused_up_gate) hit a non-dominant surface (DSV4_HC ~1.2% wall) or the same memory-bound Q4_K MoE. Hence no honest, feasible, buildable, gate-able, A/B-testable kernel hypothesis satisfies the constraints.
